title: Threats to biodiversity and ways to protect it
examples: How can we protect endangered species?

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: Does it harm or help biodiversity?

explain.say: Imagine a rainforest in the Amazon with thousands of kinds of trees, frogs, birds and insects. That huge variety of life is called biodiversity. It keeps food webs strong. But it is shrinking. Let's sort what harms it and what helps.

draw.text: Threats to biodiversity and ways to protect it

explain.say: Look at the first group, threats. The biggest is cutting down forests and draining wetlands, so animals lose their homes, their habitats. Pollution, overfishing and climate change add more pressure. Which of these have you heard about?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Does it harm or help biodiversity?

explain.say: Now see invasive species in the same list. These are living things moved to a new place where they take over. Rats brought to islands, for example, eat birds' eggs. Why might a new animal cause trouble?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Does it harm or help biodiversity?

explain.say: Now the helping groups. Nature reserves protect whole habitats, like India's tiger reserves. Seed banks store seeds, and captive breeding raises rare animals in zoos to release into the wild. Which one would you start with?

explain.say: Protecting biodiversity protects our food, medicines and clean water too. Well done! Wow fact: the Svalbard Global Seed Vault in Norway holds over a million seed samples from almost every country.

faq.a: Biodiversity is the variety of all living things in an area: the number of different species, the differences within each species, and the variety of habitats.
Mainly because of habitat loss from farming, logging and building, plus pollution, overfishing and hunting, climate change and invasive species.
asks: What are the main threats to wildlife?

faq.a: An invasive species is a living thing taken, often by people, to a new area where it spreads and harms local species, for example cane toads in Australia or rats on islands.
Seed banks dry and freeze seeds from many plants, including old crop varieties, so they can be grown again if they die out in the wild or in farms.

faq.q: How can we protect endangered species?
faq.a: By protecting their habitats in reserves, stopping hunting and illegal trade, breeding them in captivity and releasing them, and reducing pollution and climate change.
asks: How do zoos help endangered animals?

facts: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault in Norway opened in 2008 and holds over a million seed samples.
Habitat loss is the leading cause of species decline worldwide.
